newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly soft, VLCCs steady.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly soft, VLCCs steady.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were mainly soft on Friday, except very large crude carriers which managed to hold their own on good enquiry, brokers said.
Mideast/Red Sea 270,000 tonne vessels were fixed at W72.5 while to the U.K./Cont W65 was the prevailing rate.
The 260,000 tonne Erica was fixed at a firm W77 to South Korea for Yukong, while the 250,000 tonne Cosmo Delphinus was heard done at W76.5 to Japan for Idemitsu.
Brokers Galbraith's Ltd said W80 or more should be achieved in August for a part cargo of 250,000-260,000 tonnes on a modern ship going east, but that rates would fall after that.
They said there was a great shortage of modern ships to Japan and South Korea throughout August, and this should keep rates up.
They noted that last year the "hot market" ended in the second week of August and by the end of September Mideast/Japan rates had fallen from a peak of W80 to W52.5.
Suezmaxes (130,000 tonne ships), unlike VLCCs, were struggling after reaching a peak of about W95 last spring.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf voyages achieve W80 at best, with a surfeit of ships and a dearth of cargoes meaning that rates are unlikely to revive in the next week or two, brokers said.

Cross-Med Suezmaxes were even lower at about W70, but Galbraith's said firm VLCC rates may encourage charterers in the Atlantic basin to "to again turn their sights back to the Suezmax which should at least provide more cargoes."

Aframaxes (80,000 tonne vessels) were mainly steady, with cross-Med voyages continuing to fetch W110 and the inter-UKC trips around W100, although some brokers said the latter sector was likely to soften over the next week.
Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonne vessels, meanwhile, were little changed at about W120/122.5.
